notes: Read in full from The Verge.
headline: YouTube has started putting a "Made with AI" label on songs that were made mainly with generative AI tools, beginning in its YouTube Music app.
score_reason: Platform-wide labelling policy affecting listeners and artists; company announcement, no change from pool score.
importance_line: Music listeners and artists on YouTube are affected; the label will reach the main YouTube app later and YouTube may use its own detection when songs are not disclosed, so how accurate it will be is not yet known.
summary: The Verge reports that YouTube is adding a "Made with AI" label to tracks "altered or fully generated" with AI, such as songs whose composition and vocals come from a generative model, starting in the YouTube Music app and reaching the main YouTube app later. Where uploaders do not disclose AI use, YouTube says it may rely on "other signals" and its own detection tools, and the move follows Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and Bandcamp, which have each taken their own steps on AI-generated music.
